# E0140: a schema refers to another schema of the lineage

A schema reads a field of another schema through the lineage. A schema may
refer only to its own body and CUE's builtin packages: one reached through the
lineage's schemas is another schema, and this schema's meaning would then live
in that one (reference rule ref-sibling-schema). Each schema declares its own
fields.

## Example

`lineage.cue`:

```cue
lin: {
	name: "ship"
	schemas: {
		"0": "0": {
			schema: {a: int}
		}
		"0": "1": {
			schema: {a: lin.schemas["0"]["0"].schema.a, b?: int}
		}
	}
	lenses: {
		"0.1->0.0": {
			v0_1: _
			v0_0: {a: v0_1.a}
		}
	}
}
```

thema reports:

```
error[E0140]: a in schema 0.1 refers to lin.schemas["0"]["0"].schema.a, a schema in the lineage
 --> lineage.cue:8:16
  |
8 |             schema: {a: lin.schemas["0"]["0"].schema.a, b?: int}
  |                         ^^^
  |
  = note: reference rule ref-sibling-schema
  = help: a schema may refer only to its own body and CUE's builtin packages
```
